title: Willowbrook Health - SOC 2/ISO Posture Review
summary: Redwood team walked Willowbrook through SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO/SAML options, audit log retention and KMS/encryption posture. Customer requested SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO controls mapping; asked for evidence workflow and trust center invite. Next step: share docs, schedule a follow-up technical deep dive and pilot/benchmark window.
topics: SOC 2 Type II availability and timing
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
action_items: Maya: send Trust Center invite + SOC 2 Type II redacted report by 2026-12-23
Jonah: prepare controls mapping (SOC2 -> Willowbrook control IDs) and sample evidence pack by 2026-12-29
David: share current encryption/KMS questions and preferred KMS provider by 2026-12-24
Priya: confirm required log retention window (90/180/365 days) and regulatory constraints by 2026-12-24
next_steps: Redwood to share trust.redwood.ai access and redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO scope summary
Schedule technical deep dive for network/VPC and private deployment options (Jonah + infra team) week of 2027-01-04
Customer to provide prioritized compliance requirements and any third-party audit deadlines
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonah Reyes - Redwood; Sarah Nguyen (CISO), David Ortiz (Head of IT), Priya Shah (Compliance) - Willowbrook Health
---
00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for making the time, um we'll run about 45 mins, quick intro, I'm Maya with Redwood, and Jonah's our SE.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Hi Maya, hi Jonah, thanks. We wanted a posture review for SOC 2 / ISO before our Q1 audit prep.
00:20 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Great, Sarah. Quick agenda: trust center access, SOC 2 Type II artifacts, ISO 27001 scope and controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS and data residency. We'll also cover how evidence is collected.
00:35 Speaker 2 (David): Good. On our side, timeline is tight — external audit late Jan. So looking for docs and mapping this month.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): Understood. We'll start with the SOC 2. We maintain a SOC 2 Type II for our hosted services; we can share a redacted report via our trust center.
00:54 Speaker 3 (Jonah): To clarify, Willowbrook is asking for the scope — for Redwood API / hosted inference only, right, not private on-prem?
01:03 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Correct, hosted API initially; may expand to private for PHI later. Our auditors will want to see the SOC 2 for the service you provide.
01:12 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Alright. The SOC 2 covers our hosted control plane and inference runtime — note sometimes people see product names mis-typed in docs, like "Redwood Dedicated" gets written in notes as "WoodRed Dedicated" — but the scope and system descriptions are in the trust pack.
01:29 Speaker 4 (Priya): On the ISO side, do you have an ISO 27001 cert? We need an ISO controls mapping for our own ISMS.
01:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have ISO 27001 scope for the control plane and selected services; we can provide a summary of the certificate and a controls mapping matrix that maps ISO clauses to how Redwood implements them.
01:47 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Great. For evidence, auditors sometimes want configuration snapshots, access logs, and proof of change control — can you supply sample evidence or an evidence pack?
01:57 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Yes — we provide sample evidence artifacts for common controls: change management tickets, patching schedules, vulnerability scan summaries, identity provider audit logs (SSO), and sample audit logs. For production customer specifics we provide redacted versions.
02:12 Speaker 2 (David): About SSO: we use Okta; we need SAML and SCIM provisioning and RBAC so we can map roles to our internal groups. How does Redwood handle that?
02:24 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based within the Console — admin, developer, auditor — and you can map SCIM groups to those roles. We'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM docs.
02:38 Speaker 2 (David): Any limitations on SCIM attributes?
02:41 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Basic attributes supported; custom claims are limited to a few fields, sometimes names are slightly different in the SAML response, so mapping requires a quick validation.
02:52 Speaker 4 (Priya): Audit logs — retention? We need 365 days of immutable logs surfaced to a SIEM.
02:59 Speaker 1 (Maya): Default retention for the hosted logs in the Console is 90 days, but for enterprise customers we have add-ons for longer retention and can ship logs to a customer S3 or a log forwarder — or set up a dedicated logging sink.
03:12 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Important note — when streaming logs to a customer endpoint we can also configure signing and envelope encryption. For immutable storage we'd recommend the S3+WORM or a cloud provider's equivalent.
03:26 Speaker 2 (Sarah): And how about audit log integrity? Do you support append-only with tamper evidence?
03:31 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We produce logs with chronological metadata and checksums; for stronger guarantees we can enable an HSM-signed log export. We'll need to confirm with infra team for specifics.
03:44 Speaker 4 (Priya): Encryption: at rest, in transit, and KMS — do you use a customer-managed key option? We need to know if Redwood supports BYOK with our KMS.
03:54 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes — for our Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and we also support customer-managed KMS for enterprise customers where required.
04:11 Speaker 2 (David): If we use hosted API with BYOK, does that affect latency or features like caching?
04:18 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Minor overhead on key fetch, but runtime caching of decrypted keys avoids per-request KMS calls. Should be negligible for typical latencies. We'll validate in a benchmark if you want.
04:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): Also data residency — you mentioned US only, right?
04:33 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Yes, data must remain in US regions; no EU/other region processing for our PII/PHI scope.
04:40 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We have region controls and can pin processing to US regions; our trust center shows regions covered. For stricter requirements we recommend Private deployment or dedicated capacity in a US-only region.
04:53 Speaker 4 (Priya): About controls mapping: can you map Redwood control IDs to our internal control IDs and provide a matrix for auditors?
04:59 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We usually provide a mapping matrix (SOC 2/ISO -> common frameworks) and can add customer-specific control IDs if you provide them. That will be part of the action item.
05:10 Speaker 2 (David): Who is the contact for security escalations? We need an on-call contact and SLA for incident disclosure.
05:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): Our security page lists incident response contacts and timelines; for enterprise customers we include an escalation path and SLA in the contract. We'll include a summary in the trust pack.
05:28 Speaker 4 (Priya): Do you have penetration test reports or third-party attestations?
05:33 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We run annual third-party pen tests and can provide an executive summary; full reports are redacted but available under an NDA or via the trust center.
05:44 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Ok, about the trust center itself — what's the URL and access model?
05:49 Speaker 1 (Maya): trust.redwood.ai — we grant time-limited access links and can invite specific users from your Okta tenant. We manage document permissions per user and per doc.
06:00 Speaker 2 (David): Will that let us download evidence packs?
06:03 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Yes, PDF downloads are available for redacted artifacts; for direct evidence exports we can push to your S3 if needed.
06:11 Speaker 4 (Priya): Any concerns about PHI in logs or artifact exports?
06:15 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We redact customer-specific PII from shared artifacts; for customer-owned exports we can preserve full fidelity but only if you have an approved data flow and appropriate contract terms.
06:28 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Great. On certification dates — when was your latest SOC 2 Type II period end?
06:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Most recent audit period ended 2026-09-30; report was issued in November. We'll attach the redacted Type II to the trust packet.
06:44 Speaker 4 (Priya): For ISO certificate — when was it issued and what's the scope?
06:47 Speaker 1 (Maya): ISO cert issued 2025-12; scope covers control plane and hosted inference for US regions. We'll include the scope summary.
06:58 Speaker 2 (David): Back to RBAC — can we create a read-only auditor role limited to logs and config?
07:03 Speaker 3 (Jonah): Yes, there is an "auditor" role that can view logs and configurations but cannot make changes. We can also export role-based access reports for auditors.
07:14 Speaker 4 (Priya): Do you support automated evidence collection for change controls?
07:18 Speaker 3 (Jonah): We integrate with ticketing systems and can export change tickets and deployment diffs for evidence. Some smaller artifacts need manual redaction.
07:29 Speaker 2 (Sarah): This is helpful. Are there any known control gaps we should be aware of?
07:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): No critical gaps for typical SaaS use, but customers with extreme residency or specialized HSM requirements sometimes choose Private or Dedicated. We'll surface any tailored gaps in the mapping document.
07:48 Speaker 2 (David): Last question — pricing for the compliance add-ons (longer log retention, BYOK, trust center NDA access)?
07:55 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll include pricing in the follow-up — usually a line-item for log retention and a one-time setup for BYOK and private trust access.
08:05 Speaker 3 (Jonah): I'll also propose a quick pilot plan to validate logging export and KMS integration in a two-week window.
08:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Ok let's recap next steps.
08:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): Action items — Maya send trust center invite and SOC 2 redacted report by tomorrow. Jonah will produce the controls mapping and sample evidence pack; we'll aim for end of the month. David/Priya to confirm retention and KMS preference.
08:31 Speaker 2 (Sarah): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
08:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks, we'll follow up via email and set the deeper technical dive for early Jan.
08:38 Speaker 4 (Priya): Thanks.
08:40 Meeting end.
